recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a current nested-slicing validation failure can still be reproduced, file or update an issue in the active org.hl7.fhir.core validator repository with a concrete profile and instance; revisit FHIR spec prose only if a new work-group decision identifies an ambiguity.
issue_request: FHIR-15655 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request from STU3, applied for R5, asking that validation tooling support nested slicing one layer deep after a Zulip report that a nested Observation category/component slice failed with discriminator errors.
initial_application: No FHIR source commit mentioning FHIR-15655 was found in local history. The Jira was auto-approved, and the later Jira comment says Lloyd McKenzie believed the tooling problem had been addressed long ago and directed any continuing failures to the org.hl7.fhir.core validator issue tracker.
additional_context: The linked Zulip thread confirms nested slices were expected to be valid and that the observed failure was validator/IG Publisher behavior. Current Profiling FHIR source permits slicing inside existing slices and says slash-separated re-slicing names can continue indefinitely; ElementDefinition.id syntax also includes reslice names. This checkout contains no Java validator implementation.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. The current spec source already supports the nested/re-sliced slicing pattern, and the remaining implementation concern belongs in the external validator tooling repository rather than this spec source checkout.
